lead: Min-max scaling improves soft KAHM forecasting on several tasks, with a repeated approximately 20% MSE reduction on PenDigits. Logistic and Van der Pol forecasting become worse.
action: The supported revision adds a dedicated input-scaling ablation and optional preprocessing modes. Standardization remains the default because the evidence is task dependent.
confirmation_interpretation: Fresh simulation seeds repeat the harmonic, quasiperiodic, and Duffing gains and the logistic and Van der Pol regressions. Nonlinear AR changes from a very small mean degradation in the original schedule to a small improvement in confirmation. Fresh PenDigits fitting seeds repeat a 19.65% MSE reduction on the same held-out writers.
limitations_by_task: Hard KAHM assignment on PenDigits worsens by 3.96% in the original comparison and 4.14% with fresh fitting seeds. Soft KAHM still trails the stronger autoregressive and quadratic baselines on PenDigits. Scaling also changes horizon tradeoffs: the original quasiperiodic all-horizon mean improves while its horizon-12 RMSE worsens. Standard versus min-max yields identical success counts at every existing all-horizon certificate tolerance in each original and confirmation synthetic condition.
verification_summary: Every original standard-arm run matches the retained numerical record exactly after timing fields are excluded. All non-KAHM candidate results and their checked episode-score arrays remain exactly unchanged across preprocessing arms. All 33 production tests pass. Two full production replays match their frozen study counterparts in all scientific values and all 240 score arrays. Four incomplete score archives were regenerated by exact, unchanged-seed replay; all non-timing result and frozen-candidate fields matched before replacement. The damaged bytes and repair records are retained in the supplied evidence package.
repository_disposition: This revision targets the existing research/certified-soft-state-forecasting branch and draft pull request 1. It adds the revised manuscript source, complete scaling comparison summaries, reproducibility tools, and optional training-only preprocessing. Historical results and source hashes are preserved; standardization remains the default. The Git history identifies the published revision.
scope: Optional KAHM preprocessing and complete ablation; no global default replacement.
